strengths: The paper identifies a meaningful deployment-time security risk: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning and exhibit malicious behavior afterward. The white-box checkpoint-release threat model is clearly stated.

The method is simple and well motivated: pruning-score estimates separate parameters used to implant behavior from those used to suppress it. The repair-parameter survival analysis provides useful mechanistic evidence.

The evaluation covers five model families, three attack objectives, three pruning algorithms, and semi-structured pruning. Comparisons with pruned clean models help distinguish deliberate attacks from ordinary pruning-induced safety degradation.
Several effects are substantial even at 20% sparsity. The experiments on security-aware calibration and parameter restoration also provide useful initial mitigation evidence.
weaknesses: Major inconsistencies between the main results and appendix undermine confidence in model-specific findings. For content injection, Table 2 assigns Qwen ASRs of 92.2% under magnitude pruning and 99.5% under Wanda 50%, whereas Table 8 assigns those exact results to OLMo. Table 2's Llama and OLMo content-injection results similarly match rows labeled Gemma and Mistral in Table 8. These apparent labeling errors must be resolved before the evaluation can be trusted.

The utility-preservation evidence is also inconsistent. Table 1 reports Qwen's jailbreak benchmark average as 70.1 and benign refusal as 1.9%, while Table 7 reports 68.4 and 1.2%. Table 1 reports Llama's content-injection average as 67.1, versus 54.5 in Table 8. These discrepancies directly affect the central claim that the released checkpoint remains useful and inconspicuous.

The claims of consistently strong activation across pruning configurations exceed the evidence. In Table 2, Llama's SparseGPT 2:4 jailbreak ASR is 19.3%, essentially matching the clean baseline of 18.7%; its content-injection ASR under that configuration is only 4.7%. SparseGPT substantially weakens several attacks. The paper should distinguish strong results for particular configurations from broad robustness to unknown user choices.

The ablations do not establish which design choices are necessary. Varying the repair fraction is useful, but comparisons against random parameter partitions, magnitude-based selection, unrestricted injection followed by repair, and removal of KL regularization are missing. The incremental methodological contribution relative to existing transformation-triggered attacks therefore remains insufficiently isolated.

Practical deployment claims need stronger evidence. Many 50% and 2:4 configurations severely degrade benchmark utility even for clean models, limiting their attractiveness to users. The paper does not measure actual memory or latency benefits or document an end-to-end pruning-and-serving workflow sufficiently to substantiate its emphasis on practical vLLM deployment.

Evaluation uncertainty is insufficiently characterized: no repeated attack-training runs or confidence intervals are reported, harmfulness and refusal judgments rely on one model without human validation, and content injection tests only one target string. Calibration transfer is demonstrated primarily for one C4-to-WikiText pairing, which provides limited support for robustness to arbitrary calibration choices.

strengths: The paper identifies a relevant deployment security risk: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning and exhibit malicious behavior afterward. The attacker’s access and deployment assumptions are clearly stated.

The score-guided injection-and-repair method is intuitive, and several results convincingly demonstrate the phenomenon beyond ordinary pruning-induced degradation. For example, Qwen jailbreak ASR under 20% magnitude pruning rises from 8.0% for the base model to 95.7% after attack.
The evaluation covers five model families, three malicious behaviors, and seven pruning configurations, including calibration-data mismatch and semi-structured pruning.

Repair-size ablations, pruning-overlap measurements, and parameter-restoration experiments provide useful mechanistic evidence. The security-aware calibration experiments also offer a substantive initial mitigation result.
weaknesses: Material inconsistencies undermine confidence in the reported evaluation. Table 1 gives Qwen’s unpruned jailbreak utility as 70.1 and benign refusal as 1.9%, whereas Table 7 reports 68.4 and 1.2%. For Llama, benign refusal is 0.8% versus 3.9%. Table 8 appears to mislabel model blocks: the content-injection results attributed to Qwen in Table 2 appear under OLMo, and Llama’s results appear under Gemma. These discrepancies require reconciliation.

The evaluation lacks attack baselines and essential component controls. Comparisons against ordinary malicious fine-tuning followed by unrestricted repair, random parameter subsets, or magnitude-based selection would establish whether the proposed score-guided partition is necessary. Varying repair size alone does not isolate the contributions of injection selection, repair selection, and KL regularization.

Claims of consistently strong activation across pruning choices exceed the evidence. In Table 2, Llama jailbreak ASR under SparseGPT 2:4 is 19.3%, essentially unchanged from the 18.7% base rate; content-injection ASR is only 4.7%. SparseGPT results are frequently much weaker than Wanda or magnitude pruning, which matters because the threat model assumes an unknown deployment algorithm.

Practical deployment relevance needs stronger support. The manuscript repeatedly invokes vLLM integration without specifying the relevant version, compression component, or reproducible deployment commands. It provides no memory or latency measurements, and several hardware-relevant 2:4 settings substantially degrade even the base models—for example, Llama’s benchmark average falls from 67.3 to 22.1 under Wanda. Strong results at 20% sparsity remain meaningful, but broad practicality claims need qualification.

The methodological advance over existing transformation-triggered attacks is insufficiently established. Pruning is a meaningful new trigger, but the relationship between this injection-and-repair construction and prior quantization-triggered methods needs a more precise technical comparison and empirical controls.

Evaluation reliability is incompletely characterized: there are no repeated training runs or uncertainty estimates, jailbreak evaluation uses one 300-query benchmark, and LLM judgments lack human validation. Content injection tests only one target string. Although training settings and judge prompts are documented, these limitations weaken claims of broad robustness.

strengths: The paper identifies a relevant deployment-time security risk: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning but exhibit malicious behavior afterward. The threat model is clear.

The evaluation spans five model families, three attack scenarios, and multiple pruning configurations. Matched clean-model controls show that many observed effects substantially exceed the safety degradation caused by pruning alone.

Repair-set overlap measurements and parameter-restoration experiments provide useful evidence for the proposed mechanism. Security-aware calibration experiments also offer a concrete mitigation direction.
weaknesses: Substantial inconsistencies undermine confidence in the reported evaluation. Table 2 reports Qwen content-injection ASR of 24.9% under SparseGPT 20%, whereas Table 8 reports 5.3%; the complete Qwen ASR sequence from Table 2 instead appears under OLMo in Table 8. Similar apparent model-label mismatches affect other rows. Table 1 also reports Qwen jailbreak utility/benign refusal as 70.1/1.9, versus 68.4/1.2 in Table 7. These discrepancies require reconciliation.

The methodological contribution is insufficiently isolated. There are no comparisons against ordinary sequential malicious/benign fine-tuning, random parameter partitions, or alternative score-based selections, and no ablation of the KL regularizer. Varying the repair fraction alone does not establish which proposed components are necessary or how much they improve over simpler approaches.

Claims of consistently strong activation across pruning configurations overstate the evidence. For Llama with SparseGPT 2:4, jailbreak ASR is 19.3% versus 18.7% for the clean model, and content-injection ASR is only 4.7%. Such cases materially qualify the claimed robustness to an unknown pruning configuration.

Deployment practicality is incompletely established. Several 2:4 configurations severely degrade utility; for example, the attacked Llama jailbreak model averages 20.2 under Wanda 2:4 versus 66.4 unpruned. No measured memory or latency benefits, or precise deployment software versions, substantiate the practical compression narrative.

Evaluation uncertainty is unquantified: no repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or human validation of the LLM judge are reported. Generalization is tested with one main calibration-dataset transfer, one harmful-query benchmark, and one target string. These limitations, together with the reporting discrepancies and missing methodological controls, leave the submission below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: The paper identifies a meaningful deployment-time vulnerability: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning yet exhibit malicious behavior afterward. The threat model clearly separates adversarial checkpoint preparation from subsequent user-controlled pruning.

The central phenomenon is convincingly demonstrated against matched, pruned base-model controls. For example, Qwen jailbreak ASR under 20% magnitude pruning rises from 8.0% to 95.7%, while the attacked unpruned model remains near its original ASR.

Evaluation is broad: five model families, additional 14B and 32B Qwen models, three malicious behaviors, three pruning algorithms, and multiple sparsity configurations. Calibration-distribution changes and subsequent quantization provide useful robustness checks.

The mechanism receives supporting evidence from repair-set ablations, measurements of which repaired weights are pruned, and oracle restoration experiments. Security-aware calibration and fine-tuning experiments also provide concrete defensive insights.
weaknesses: The incremental contribution over existing transformation-activated attacks is insufficiently isolated. There are no matched random-mask, unrestricted injection/repair, or alternative scoring baselines. Varying mask sizes does not establish how much the proposed score-based partition contributes beyond sequential malicious training and repair.

Claims of consistently strong activation across pruning methods overstate the results. Llama jailbreak ASR under SparseGPT 2:4 is 19.3%, versus 18.7% for the base model; Qwen-32B content-injection ASR under the same configuration is only 0.6%. SparseGPT content-injection results are also weak for Gemma and Mistral. These limitations should be prominent in the abstract and conclusions.

Utility preservation needs more careful qualification. The attacked unpruned Qwen jailbreak model loses 11.6 percentage points on GSM8K, which is obscured by averaging across benchmarks. Several 2:4 configurations have extremely poor coding and mathematics performance even before accounting for the attack, limiting their deployment relevance. Strong results at 20% sparsity remain persuasive.

Statistical and measurement validation is limited. No repeated training runs or confidence intervals are reported; Table 1's standard deviations across different benchmarks do not establish statistical equivalence. Jailbreak and refusal judgments rely on one LLM evaluator without reported human validation or agreement with another judge.

Reproducibility and practical positioning need strengthening. The appendix supplies useful training details, but exact pruning software versions, implementation configurations, optimizer details, and computational costs are not clearly documented. The repeated attribution of pruning and sparse fine-tuning to vLLM should identify the actual compression tooling and supported deployment path. The claimed code release cannot be verified from the supplied manuscript's blank link.

strengths: The paper identifies a meaningful deployment security risk: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning yet exhibit malicious behavior afterward. The threat model is explicit, and the proposed mechanism is clear and technically plausible.

The central phenomenon is supported by substantial experiments across five model families, three attack objectives, and three pruning algorithms, with additional 14B/32B experiments. Comparisons against identically pruned clean models help distinguish the attack from ordinary pruning-induced safety degradation.

Several results demonstrate large effects while retaining useful model performance. For example, Qwen jailbreak ASR under 20% Wanda pruning increases from 9.3% for the clean model to 93.0% for the attacked model, while their average utility scores remain similar.

The analysis goes beyond headline success rates: it examines parameter-selection ratios, actual removal of repaired weights, calibration distribution shifts, mitigation strategies, and subsequent fine-tuning and quantization. The successful security-aware fine-tuning experiment is particularly informative.
weaknesses: The method lacks important comparative controls. Clean-model baselines establish the vulnerability, but random parameter masks, magnitude-based selection, and unrestricted injection/repair baselines are absent. Consequently, the experiments do not adequately isolate the benefit of Wanda-based parameter partitioning. The methodological advance over existing transformation-activated attacks also needs sharper positioning.

Claims of consistently strong activation across pruning methods exceed the evidence. Llama jailbreak ASR under SparseGPT 2:4 is 19.3%, versus 18.7% for its clean baseline; Mistral content-injection ASR under SparseGPT 20% is only 1.7%. Larger-model transfer also weakens substantially for some SparseGPT settings. These exceptions should qualify the abstract, Table 2 caption, and conclusions.

Utility preservation is overstated when summarized across benchmarks. For the unpruned Qwen jailbreak model, GSM8K falls from 80.1% to 68.5%. Some hardware-relevant 2:4 configurations also have very poor absolute utility, partly attributable to pruning itself. The practical deployment argument would benefit from clearly separating viable operating points and reporting actual memory or throughput benefits.

Evaluation uncertainty is insufficiently characterized. There are no repeated training runs or confidence intervals, and the standard deviations in Table 1 describe variation across benchmarks rather than experimental uncertainty. Jailbreak and refusal judgments rely on one automated evaluator without reported human validation. Content injection tests only one target string, limiting conclusions about broader targeted manipulation.

The mitigation results support narrower conclusions than the discussion sometimes suggests. Security-aware calibration nearly eliminates jailbreak ASR for SparseGPT, and security-aware fine-tuning suppresses it while improving utility in the tested setting. These are useful positive results, but their generality remains unclear because the defense data comes from the same source used for attack training, and fine-tuning is evaluated on only one model and attack scenario.

strengths: The paper identifies a meaningful deployment-time security vulnerability: a checkpoint can appear benign before pruning yet exhibit malicious behavior afterward. This extends transformation-triggered attacks to an important compression setting.

The central phenomenon is convincingly demonstrated against matched unattacked models. For example, Qwen2.5 jailbreak ASR under 20% Wanda pruning increases from 9.3% to 93.0%, while the attacked unpruned model remains close to the original safety level.

The evaluation is broad: five model families, additional 14B and 32B models, three attack objectives, three pruning algorithms, multiple sparsity patterns, and mismatched calibration datasets. Five utility benchmarks and benign-refusal measurements help distinguish malicious activation from general model degradation.

The mechanism receives useful empirical support through parameter-selection ablations, measurements of repair-weight removal, and restoration experiments. Security-aware calibration, subsequent fine-tuning, and quantization experiments provide additional practical insight.
weaknesses: Claims of consistently strong activation across configurations overstate the evidence. In Table 2, Llama3.1 jailbreak ASR under SparseGPT 2:4 is 19.3%, versus 18.7% for the unattacked baseline. Content-injection ASR is also low in several SparseGPT settings, including 0.6% for Qwen2.5-32B under 2:4 pruning. The conclusions should distinguish a demonstrated vulnerability from reliable activation under unknown pruning choices.

The evaluation lacks direct comparisons with simpler attack constructions, such as random parameter partitions or unrestricted injection followed by repair. Varying partition sizes does not establish the incremental value of importance-based selection. The methodological advance over prior transformation-triggered attacks consequently remains less well isolated than the vulnerability itself.

Utility preservation is presented too categorically. Before pruning, Qwen2.5 jailbreak training reduces GSM8K from 80.1% to 68.5%, despite a relatively small average benchmark decline. Many 2:4 configurations also have severe utility losses, limiting their deployment relevance. Strong results at 20% pruning remain persuasive, but hardware memory or throughput measurements would better substantiate the practical compression framing.

Statistical and evaluator validation are limited. The paper reports no repeated-training variability or confidence intervals, and Table 1's standard deviation across benchmarks does not quantify experimental uncertainty. Jailbreak and refusal outcomes rely on one LLM judge without reported human agreement; content injection is evaluated using only one target string.

The analysis does not fully explain why SparseGPT can suppress activation despite removing almost all repair parameters. Moreover, security-aware calibration nearly eliminates jailbreak ASR for SparseGPT, and brief safety fine-tuning does so in the tested Qwen setting. These are valuable findings, but they warrant more qualified claims about robustness and clearer discussion of the conditions under which the threat persists.
